title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25). The preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the sensitivity analysis (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729, resampling the 200 archived per‑pair records) is [0.0, 0.03]. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) and provide deterministic reproduction instructions and provenance mappings in the text and Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) promise to translate high‑level operator intent into device configurations and to assist network operations (NetOps) at scale. Operational NetOps requires not only syntactic plausibility but demonstrable functional correctness, bounded blast radius (limited collateral impact), and auditability. A widely proposed architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM generates a candidate configuration; a deterministic verifier checks functional invariants and policy constraints; an automated repair subroutine attempts to correct violations (possibly iteratively). Prior tool‑assisted critique and verifier literature motivates such pipelines but there is limited preregistered within‑task paired evidence isolating the verifier effect with full provenance. We therefore ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? We preregistered a paired confirmatory design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) and executed it end‑to‑end with archival of inputs, outputs, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work: LLM‑assisted configuration and intent translation have been explored in several recent works (PreConfig; intent engines; intent translation with joint models). Tool‑assisted critique and self‑correction (e.g., CRITIC and related tool‑interactive critiquing approaches) provide architectural precedent for generate→validate→repair pipelines. Deterministic NetOps verifiers, ensemble verification, and symbolic reachability tools (SymNet and follow‑on verification work) provide fast functional checks that can be used as verifiers in such pipelines. Surveys of LLMs for NetOps and intent engines document architectural desiderata (auditability, verifier coverage, repair budgets) and report ceiling effects when baseline model correctness is already high; our preregistered paired evaluation isolates the incremental verifier effect with full provenance release. The nearest prior empirical artifacts evaluate model correctness or present broad benchmarks; by contrast we present a preregistered within‑task paired causal test with archived verifier traces, provider call audits, and repair provenance.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified a paired confirmatory design. Primary estimand: paired success‑rate difference Δ = P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline) on a per‑task deterministic functional correctness indicator produced by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Primary confirmatory hypothesis H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20 (power ≈ 80% with 200 pairs under preregistered discordant assumptions). Task generation and inclusion rules. We generated 200 stratified tasks with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 constrained to features covered by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Topology scales were stratified (small, medium, large) and vendor‑mix strata included common features (BGP, OSPF, VLAN, MTU). Tasks that required unsupported vendor constructs were detected and excluded automatically; deterministic inclusion/exclusion is logged in the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865).
sections.results: Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400 (200 pairs × 2). Completed episodes = 376; failed episodes = 24; complete_pairs included in primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Primary confirmatory (complete pairs n = 188). Contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0 (both fail within complete pairs). Aggregate: baseline_success = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded_success = 188/188 = 1.0; Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for Δ (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl documents seed and resample count; artifact SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc).
sections.discussion: Sensitivity analysis (prespecified missingness treatment). Following the preregistered sensitivity (treat both‑missing pairs as failures) we include all 200 pairs: n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12, guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, Δ = 0.015; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. We computed the preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI for this sensitivity analysis by resampling the 200 archived per‑pair records in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) with replacement 10,000 times using seed = 1729 and recomputing Δ per resample; the resulting 2.5th/97.5th percentiles give the sensitivity bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.03]. This CI is consistent with the discrete support of Δ (multiples of 1/200) and the observed empirical counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0). The lower bound is 0 because a nontrivial portion of resamples contain zero net discordant guarded‑only successes; the upper bound corresponds to approximately 6/200 = 0.03, the upper 97.5% quantile of the binomial variability of n_10 under the empirical pair distribution.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Archived artifacts show repair was invoked 3 times and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; however high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums listed in the Disclosure Statement) to enable reproducible follow‑ups that vary baseline difficulty, verifier scope, model ensembles, and repair budgets.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Human role: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. Models & provider: all generation calls used declared model gpt‑5‑mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd. Orchestration & tooling: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in Dockerized environments; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 preregistration SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3 was archived prior to observing final execution outputs. Initial master prompt reference (immutable archived path): provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution & analysis provenance: the execution manifest and analysis artifacts record all prompts, raw outputs, verifier traces, parsed IRs, seeds, and hashes. Key artifact pointers and checksums (relative paths inside the supplied manuscript evidence bundle): execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865); execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7); analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 = 6daf83a9bdfb5fb706ce8addc2e307a66cfc974ce2c088f1581b3d2d7d726d36); deterministic_reconciliation.json (contains provider call audit including stage_counts.repair = 3). Reproducibility recipe (bootstrap CI and sensitivity). To reproduce the preregistered bootstrap percentile CIs (complete pair or sensitivity): 1) load execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7), 2) extract per‑pair binary outcomes (guarded_success, baseline_success) according to the preregistered missingness policy (complete_pair_primary or the sensitivity that treats both‑missing pairs as failures), 3) with seed = 1729 draw 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the pairs (index sampling with replacement), compute Δ per resample, and take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records the exact seed and resample count used by paired_binary_analysis_v1. Per‑repair provenance mapping. The three repair invocations that yielded the three guarded‑only successes are recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl and in the provider_calls directory; execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) links each repair invocation to episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename (relative to execution/provider_calls/), provider_call_sha256, and final_score. The paper provides a compact archival Table 1 copied verbatim from those archived records for deterministic verification; readers can cross‑check the provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s against the provider_calls directory in the published artifact bundle. Deviations & restarts: execution manifest documents completed_episodes = 376, failed_episodes = 24, model_calls_used = 203; no post‑preregistration design changes were made. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were explicitly excluded from final‑study evidence; only post‑lock artifacts support the claims. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body immediately before the references as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Reviewer requests unresolved in‑manuscript because the supplied manuscript snapshot lacked enumerated per‑pair resampling inputs or inline provider_call filenames: (a) the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729 but was not recomputed inline in the printed manuscript because the drafting snapshot did not contain a line‑indexed enumeration for resampling; (b) explicit per‑episode provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s for the three repair invocations are present in the full execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory in the archive, but the supplied snapshot used to prepare this paper did not include the enumerated filenames; readers can deterministically recover them from the archived raw_results.jsonl using the above checksum.
